title: Skybase's primitives fall into three lifecycle classes distinguished by activation status plus invocability
content:
Reading the Global Activation Status alongside the In Progress Invocations Directory across A.6.1.1.4.2.2 and A.6.1.1.4.2.3 reveals three distinct classes, not two.

**Completed one-shots**: Genesis Primitives whose work is finished — status `Completed`, no further Invocation possible.

**Active singletons**: status `Active`, but "deployed only once, [so] no further Instances of the Primitive can be Invoked" — the Root Edit Primitive (A.6.1.1.4.2.2.2.1.1 / .1.4), the Ecosystem Upkeep Fee Primitive (A.6.1.1.4.2.3.1.1.1 / .1.4) and the Upkeep Rebate Primitive (A.6.1.1.4.2.3.2.1.1 / .1.4). One perpetual Instance carries a standing capability; there is nothing to add and nothing to finish.

**Repeatable primitives**: live In Progress directories that genuinely route work, with success moving a subtree into Active Instances — the Executor Accord Primitive (A.6.1.1.4.2.2.1.4) and the Light Agent Primitive (A.6.1.1.4.2.2.3.4), the latter currently `Inactive` with no Instances at all.

The distinction matters for reading any Agent Artifact. "Single Instance" does not imply finished, and `Inactive` does not imply single-use: Skybase's ability to amend itself and its obligation to pay upkeep are permanent singletons, while its Accords and Light Agents are the parts designed to be added to over time. An observer wanting to know where an Agent can still grow should look at which primitives keep an open Invocation directory.
